jobs.title: Data & AI Transformation Director
jobs.description:
At PwC, our people in integration and platform architecture focus on designing and implementing seamless integration solutions and robust platform architectures for clients. They enable efficient data flow and optimise technology infrastructure for enhanced business performance. Those in integration architecture at PwC will focus on designing and implementing seamless integration solutions to connect various organisational systems and applications. Your work will involve creating robust architectures that enable efficient data flow and enhance overall business processes.

The Opportunity

As a Data & AI Transformation Director, unlock your potential and embrace the chance to drive meaningful outcomes that’ll elevate your career. We are seeking a Director, Data & AI Transformation - Microsoft Practice to lead and deliver large-scale Microsoft-based transformation programs across cloud, data, analytics, and artificial intelligence. This individual will be responsible for owning end-to-end program delivery, managing executive stakeholder relationships, building high-performing delivery teams, and helping grow PwC's Microsoft consulting practice.

The successful candidate will combine deep expertise in Microsoft technologies, particularly Microsoft Azure and Microsoft AI Foundry, with proven experience leading large-scale enterprise transformation programs and offshore delivery organizations. This is a delivery-first leadership role focused on execution, client outcomes, and scaling delivery capabilities rather than pure sales or advisory responsibilities. Your role will include, but isn’t limited to:

Delivery Leadership & Program Ownership

Lead end-to-end delivery of large-scale Microsoft Data, AI, and Cloud transformation programs.
Own program outcomes including scope, budget, governance, risk management, quality, and delivery success.
Lead multiple concurrent programs and workstreams across complex enterprise environments.
Establish effective delivery governance, escalation management, and executive reporting structures.
Drive successful outcomes across strategic transformation initiatives and managed delivery engagements.

Microsoft Data & AI Transformation

Lead delivery of solutions leveraging: Microsoft Azure; Microsoft AI Foundry; Azure AI Services; Microsoft Fabric; Enterprise Data Platforms; Modern Analytics Solutions.
Support clients in cloud modernization, data platform transformation, and enterprise AI adoption initiatives.
Develop delivery roadmaps that align technology investments with business objectives and measurable outcomes.
Provide practical guidance on enterprise Data & AI transformation approaches and operating models.

Executive Stakeholder Management

Build trusted advisor relationships with CIOs, CTOs, Chief Data Officers, technology leaders, and business executives.
Represent PwC during executive steering committees, governance reviews, and program leadership meetings.
Serve as the primary delivery lead for strategic client engagements.
Communicate delivery status, risks, dependencies, and business impacts to executive stakeholders.
Facilitate decision-making across client, partner, and delivery teams.

Global Delivery & Offshore Leadership

Lead geographically distributed teams across Canada, the United States, and offshore delivery centres.
Manage complex global delivery models utilizing onshore and offshore resources.
Coordinate activities across delivery teams, vendors, architects, engineers, and business stakeholders.
Establish delivery practices that support scalability, quality, accountability, and operational excellence.
Drive issue resolution, risk mitigation, and program recovery efforts where required.

Talent Development & Practice Growth

Build and scale high-performing delivery teams.
Leverage professional networks to identify, attract, and develop top Microsoft delivery talent.
Mentor Managers, Senior Managers, Architects, and Delivery Leaders.
Foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, transparency, and continuous improvement.
Contribute to the ongoing growth of PwC's Microsoft Data & AI practice.

Business Development & Alliance Growth

Support pursuits, proposals, executive presentations, and solution development activities.
Build and strengthen relationships with Microsoft and key client stakeholders.
Contribute to thought leadership and market-facing initiatives related to Microsoft Data & AI solutions.
Help develop delivery offerings, accelerators, and go-to-market capabilities.
Support long-term practice growth and strategic expansion objectives.

What You'll Bring

Your skills, knowledge, and experiences are what set you apart. Here's what we look for:

12+ years of professional experience in technology consulting, enterprise transformation, cloud delivery, or technology leadership.
10+ years of experience leading large-scale enterprise technology programs and delivery organizations.
Proven experience delivering Microsoft-based transformation programs.
Strong experience with Microsoft Azure and modern Microsoft Data & AI technologies.
Extensive experience managing offshore and global delivery teams.
Demonstrated success managing executive-level stakeholder relationships and steering committees.
Experience leading large multidisciplinary teams across delivery, architecture, engineering, and business functions.
Strong consulting, stakeholder management, and client relationship management capabilities.
Experience owning complex budgets, delivery risks, resource plans, and program governance.
Demonstrated ability to independently lead large-scale client engagements with limited oversight.

This position ensures continuity and upholds our standards of excellence following the departure of a valued team member.

The salary range for this position is $191,200 - $241,200. The posted salary range represents the expected hiring range for PwC locations in major city centres. Given our national recruiting approach, ranges may vary for positions in other locations. At PwC Canada, base salary is determined by your skills, experience, qualifications and work location. In addition to base salary, eligible employees may have opportunities to participate in variable incentive pay programs which are designed to reward individual and firm-wide achievements. We are committed to offering competitive compensation and adhere to all relevant pay transparency legislation. During the hiring process, our Talent Acquisition team will provide details about our comprehensive total rewards package.

Why you’ll love PwC

We’re inspiring and empowering our people to change the world. Powered by the latest technology, you’ll be a part of diverse teams helping public and private clients build trust and deliver sustained outcomes. This meaningful work, and our continuous development environment, will take your career to the next level. We reward your impact, and support your wellbeing, through a competitive compensation package, inclusive benefits and flexibility programs that will help you thrive in work and life. Learn more about our Application Process and Total Rewards Package at: https://jobs-ca.pwc.com/ca/en/life-at-pwc

jobs.title: Director of GTM Data, Processes, and AI Enablement
jobs.description:
MaintainX is a leading mobile-first work execution platform
for industrial and frontline teams. More than 13,000 customers
, including Duracell, McDonald's, Shell, DHL and Volvo, use MaintainX to cut unplanned downtime and run better operations, across 13.9 million managed assets and 79.5 million completed work orders.

In August 2026 MaintainX became part of Autodesk, joining
Autodesk Operations Solutions
, the organization unifying Autodesk's operations platform alongside Tandem, FlexSim and Fusion Operations.
Autodesk's strategy is to converge design, make and operate into one continuous lifecycle: design an asset, build it, run it, then feed what you learn running it back into the next design. Autodesk had design and make. Operate is the phase that tells you what actually happened, and it is ours.

The Role

MaintainX (part of Autodesk) is hiring a Director of GTM Data, Processes, and AI Enablement to own critical foundations of our GTM teams, including:

Customer and prospect data within our CRM;
Core CRM processes that enable selling across GTM teams (e.g., opportunity workflows, territory assignment processes); and
Our internal GenAI and automation efforts driving efficiency, effectiveness, and productivity of our GTM teams

This role also owns the integration of the MaintainX GTM teams into Autodesk GTM systems, processes, and GTM motions, for the core functional areas of the role – a key area of focus for the next 6 to 18 months.

The role sits in the broader MaintainX Revenue Strategy and Operations team and leads a small team of data quality analysts, but we expect this role to drive the majority of its impact through others outside of their direct team. Across all functional areas, this role will be working with, influencing, and directing the work of senior stakeholders, front-line managers, and ICs across Marketing, Rev Ops, Enablement, and GTM Engineering. We need someone with deep functional expertise that knows best practices and has rapid pattern recognition for solutions to GTM issues, who is technical enough to be credible with engineers, and is practical enough to be trusted by sellers to get work done.

What You'll Do

Own CRM data quality and governance

Set the strategy, standards, and governance for leads, contacts, accounts, and account hierarchies. That includes parent/child structures, holding companies, franchises, PE portfolios, and multi-site customers.
Move data quality from cleanup to prevention. Put in intake controls, matching and dedupe rules, and enrichment precedence, and track them on a data quality scorecard with targets.
Show leadership what data gaps cost in revenue, and make GTM data ready for AI use cases.
Lead the team doing this work, including writing requirements for GTM Systems to implement.
Develop deduplication strategies and processes to manage a dual CRM environment across MaintainX and Autodesk

Drive core CRM-based processes and workflows

Own CRM territory management developing the processes and systems requirements to implement the territory design and strategy defined by GTM leadership and Rev Ops teams.
Own our rules of engagement: account ownership, crediting, and conflict resolution across segments, regions, and teams – including both MaintainX selling in isolation and coordination between MaintainX and Autodesk sellers
Own optimization of CRM processes and workflows for end user teams, including building an understanding of current processes, identifying points of improvement, working with GTM systems and Rev Ops teams to define business requirements
Collaborate with Rev Ops, Enablement, and GTM systems teams to ensure field teams know how to use our systems and processes as they change, through release communications, training, and documentation.

Lead the GTM AI program for field teams

Run out GenAI and automation program for GTM field teams end to end: intake, prioritization and resource allocation across GTM and Engineering, operating cadences, solution evaluation, executive readouts, field enablement.
Lead discovery with Sales leaders to find the highest-value automation and agent opportunities. Align leadership and our GTM engineering team on one prioritized roadmap.
Own business requirements, build-vs-buy recommendations, and testing for centrally built solutions. Partner with Engineering to build and launch them.
Set the standards for how teams build their own solutions: knowledge base governance, a quality bar, and a path for scaling proven team-built tools across the org.
Own rollout with Enablement and measure adoption and ROI. The measure is workflows changed, not trainings delivered.

Lead integration efforts for MaintainX GTM into Autodesk

Own the GTM integration plan, governance and coordination across the workstreams, including: systems and data, account mapping and ownership, territories, sales process alignment, rules of engagement for joint selling, and enablement.
Coordinate stakeholders across both organizations. Run the cadence, track risks and dependencies, and escalate decisions.
Be accountable for integration outcomes, not just coordination.

About You

10+ years in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, or GTM strategy at a B2B SaaS company, including 3+ years leading people.
Deep expertise in core sales processes, territory design, and rules of engagement.
Strong command of the CRM data model: Salesforce objects, account hierarchies, matching, and enrichment. You define and specify; you don't need to configure.
Hands-on experience bringing AI into GTM workflows (LLMs, agents, workflow automation), with results you can measure. Fluent enough to work credibly with engineers.
A track record of leading large cross-functional programs through influence, including with VP and C-level leaders.
M&A or GTM integration experience is strongly preferred.
Clear writing and speaking. You can make complex tradeoffs understandable to sellers, engineers, and executives.

Our mission is to keep the physical world running.
Factories, fleets, hospitals and campuses stay up because the people who maintain them have tools worth using. That is what we build.

Compensation and benefits.
Base pay is one part of the package. Depending on the role, compensation may also include commission, an annual bonus and equity. Benefits differ by country. For roles in the United States, Autodesk’s benefits are described at benefits.autodesk.com. For roles in Canada and other countries, the plan differs on health coverage, retirement and leave, and your recruiter will walk you through it.

Belonging.
We take pride in a culture where everyone can thrive. More at autodesk.com/company/global-belonging. More on where this is going: Autodesk CEO Andrew Anagnost on building the future of connected operations, and AOS SVP Stephen Hooper on welcoming MaintainX to Autodesk.

jobs.title: Vice President Finance, Americas
jobs.description:
The Vice President, Finance, Americas is responsible for providing strategic financial leadership and oversight across the Americas region. This role partners with executive and business leaders to drive financial performance, support growth initiatives, ensure compliance with financial and regulatory requirements, and deliver accurate financial planning, reporting, and analysis. The VP Finance leads regional finance functions, including accounting, budgeting, forecasting, tax, treasury, internal controls, and financial operations, while fostering a high-performing team and supporting the achievement of organizational objectives.

Reports to the Chief Financial Officer.

Responsibilities

1. Financial Reporting & Accounting

Oversee accounting operations for the Americas region, including general ledger, month-end/quarter-end closing, and consolidation.
Own inventory accounting for the Memphis distribution center — valuation methodology, standard costing, cycle counts, and obsolescence/reserve policy.
Ensure COGS accuracy and margin analysis tied to distribution operations.
Ensure accuracy of financial statements prepared in accordance with local GAAP in each jurisdiction (US, Canada, and LatAm countries).
Prepare and submit financial reports in compliance with IFRS and Group accounting standards, ensuring quality and compliance.
Coordinate with external auditors for annual audits, implement improvement plans, and maintain effective communication with internal and external audit teams.
Work closely with the HQ finance team to ensure consistency in reporting formats, policies, and processes.

2. Compliance

Maintain and enhance internal control and accounting procedures to align with Group policies and US/Canadian/LatAm regulations.
Ensure customs and bonded warehouse compliance — duty deferral, in-bond transfers, and CBP requirements — for the Memphis distribution center, partnering with trade compliance and logistics teams.
Ensure compliance with local direct and indirect tax regulations, including corporate income tax, VAT/GST, and multi-state US sales/use tax nexus; complete filings accurately and on time.
Regularly review the reasonableness of intercompany transfer pricing across US, Canada, and LatAm entities, and assess associated risks.

3. Treasury & Financial Planning

Manage cash flow, working capital, and banking relationships across the Americas to ensure liquidity and efficient funding.
Support financing activities and treasury optimization.
Provide budgeting, forecasting, and financial analysis to support operational decision-making across HQ, sales & marketing offices, and the distribution center.

4. System & Process Enhancement

Drive ERP system integration and automation to improve reporting efficiency, data accuracy, and close timelines.
Identify process improvement opportunities across order-to-cash and purchase-to-pay to enhance timeliness and reliability of financial information.

Qualifications and Experience

Bachelor's degree or above in Accounting, Finance, or related field; CPA/ACA/ACCA qualification preferred.
Minimum 15 years of accounting or finance experience, including at least 6 years in a managerial or Controller role.
Solid knowledge of IFRS, US/Canadian tax regulations, compliance, and internal controls.
Experience with distribution or logistics operations, including inventory accounting and customs/bonded warehouse environments, strongly preferred.
Hands-on SAP experience, particularly ERP implementation or migration, is a strong plus.
Previous experience in multinational or listed companies is a strong plus.
Proven leadership experience building and managing multi-country/multi-entity finance teams.
Strong written and verbal English communication skills for global stakeholder management. Chinese is a plus for Group-level communication.

Competencies (Skills & Behaviors)

Strong AI awareness with hands-on experience implementing AI tools or automation workflows within a finance environment.
Experience supporting regional or global finance functions.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Familiar with transfer pricing and cross-border tax principles.
Comfortable operating at senior leadership/executive committee level, with strong stakeholder management and influencing skills.
Familiar with inventory and sales/purchase management.

Leadership & Strategic Influence

Partner with Americas business, sales, and marketing leadership to provide financial insights, operational performance analysis, and cost control recommendations.
Build, lead, and develop a high-performing finance team across Montreal HQ, sales & marketing offices, and the Memphis distribution center; drive talent development and succession planning.
Act as a strategic finance partner to the Americas leadership team, contributing to regional business strategy, investment decisions, and capital allocation.
Report to the Group CFO on financial performance, risks, and strategic priorities, representing Americas Finance in Group-level executive discussions.

jobs.title: Director of Financial Planning and Analysis
jobs.description:
About the Company

Our client is a leading capital markets organization. They are looking for a Director, Corporate FP&A who will be responsible for leading the Corporate FP&A team responsible for enterprise planning, while also playing a key role in supporting Finance Business Partnering (FBP) teams.
In this leadership role, you empower financially sound planning and decision-making throughout the organization. You do this by spreading financial acumen, telling compelling, data-driven stories to spur action, bridging the knowledge gap between Finance and Operations, and assisting in the creation of FP&A decision-support tools. You will simplify FP&A analysis into easily digestible business logic and take a more technology-guided and teaching-focused approach to business partnering, enabling decision-makers to make sound financial decisions more independently

Requirements

CPA designation or similar (MBA/CFA)
10-15+ years of progressive finance experience with main focus in FP&A
Exposure to IFRS at a public listed entity
Strong business partnering with board reporting experience
Experience in a multi-entity environment with complex organization structures

Salary Range

$160,000 - $180,000/year

Why Work Here

High visibility with CEO, CFO and Board
Enterprise-wide impact as acquisitions has outpaced finance processes
This hire would ideally hit VPs succession map
Exposure to investor relations and strategic finance

About the Opportunity

Enterprise Planning

Ownership of forecasting and annual business planning across the group, including:
Coordination of timelines and assumption alignment across business units
Multi-stage reviews with senior leadership
Creation of final presentations for the Board of Directors
Ownership of Adaptive Planning (Workday Planning tool)
Lead the corporate target-setting process to optimize investment allocation while establishing achievable and stretch performance targets that drive desired behaviours and outcomes
Ownership of the long-term strategic forecast model used in the annual strategic planning process and longer-term modelling
Conduct business analysis on key enterprise performance drivers (e.g., headcount, profitability)

Corporate Performance Reporting

Accountable for corporate performance reporting to senior management and the Board of Directors, with a focus on forward-looking, actionable insights
Responsible for content creation, key messaging, and performance insights
Lead presentations of results to the Operating Committee
Accountable for operating segment reporting in external financial statements and MD&A
Partner closely with Investor Relations to synthesize monthly performance data into:
Quarterly earnings scripts
Q&A preparation materials
Analyst consensus models
Investor presentation metrics
Prepare supplementary schedules and analyze/proof quarterly and annual MD&A, press releases, Investor Relations presentations, and communications with shareholders and analysts
Partner closely with other Finance leaders and teams to improve data capture and GL reporting structures and optimize straight-through processing
Ownership of incentive plan performance measurement and associated liabilities across TMX; contribute to the design of incentive plans in partnership with HR

Enterprise Portfolio Governance

Oversee and recommend processes for annual and in-year discretionary investment allocations that balance governance, transparency, and business outcomes in alignment with TMX's growth strategy
Facilitate transparency for material new initiatives outside approved budgets to support CEO, CFO, and SMT approval decisions
Partner with the PMO and Integration Management Office on overall project governance and tracking
Co-owner of company-wide policies, including the TMX Expenditure and Budget Authorization Policy

Cost Allocation (Shared Services) Model

Ownership of the enterprise-wide cost allocation framework across legal entities and operating segments
Lead the design and structure of the model, including:
Tools
Principles
Governance
Regulatory compliance
Tax compliance
Provide detailed transparency to senior management and Business Unit FBPs regarding key drivers and outcomes, with a focus on understanding value delivery and influencing shared services costs
Provide variance analysis (budget vs. actual, prior period comparisons, etc.) in a manner that is easily understood by senior management
Support FBPs in stakeholder discussions to improve confidence in model integrity
Partner closely with team members to enhance data capture and GL reporting structures and improve straight-through processing
Conduct business analysis on key enterprise cost drivers
Enhance the rigour and control framework surrounding model updates and design
Build flexibility and adaptability into the model to accommodate a rapidly evolving corporate structure, including M&A activity
Collaborate with external auditors during quarterly reviews and annual audits
Improve efficiency of model updates and monthly/quarterly journal entries through automation where possible
Develop a roadmap for the next generation of the model and framework

Other

Ownership of quarterly and annual goodwill impairment testing and valuation processes, including:
Alignment with strategic plans
Input into external disclosure requirements
Partner with Corporate Strategy and Strategic Finance teams to advance enterprise analysis and insight generation
Champion and participate in knowledge-sharing forums for FBPs and FP&A professionals to exchange best practices on educating business leaders through FP&A decision-support processes
Assist in defining success criteria for FP&A tools and establishing measurable business and technical metrics to monitor utilization and quality

jobs.title: Director, Digital Safety
jobs.description:
Are you looking for a role where you can define the future of digital safety in a complex, mission-critical environment? Can you see yourself leading enterprise-wide cybersecurity programs while establishing the standards, controls, and governance frameworks that protect critical digital systems and information assets? If you answered yes, this may be the job for you. Apply today,
as our Chalk River location is looking for a Director, Digital Safety
to lead the development and implementation of CNL's Digital Safety Framework.

What you will be doing!

Digital Safety Framework & Standards Authority
Defining, maintaining, and evolving the enterprise Digital Safety Framework, incorporating nuclear safety principles such as defence-in-depth, graded approach, and continuous improvement.
Establishing and governing mandatory, non-negotiable digital safety control requirements applicable to:
Information systems
Operational technologies
Nuclear-related digital assets
Identity and access managemen
Data protection and asset lifecycle management

Translating external standards (CSA N290.7, ISO 27001, NIST, IAEA) into a cohesive, internally consistent Digital Safety Framework.
Defining the baseline conditions required for safe digital operations, ensuring clarity in expectations across all business and operational areas.

Program Implementation
Embedding Digital Safety requirements into all business processes, projects, and operational activities to obtain compliance with defined safety standards.
Developing and delivering enterprise-wide programs to build digital safety awareness, competency, and behavioural accountability.
Driving the integration of human factors and behavioural science into digital safety practices, reinforcing safe decision-making and risk-awareness across the workforce.
Promoting and enforcing understanding so that all employees and contractors understand their role in maintaining digital safety and operate within defined safety expectations.

Control Oversight and Operational Assurance
Exercising authority to mandate that all digital systems and activities comply with established Digital Safety requirements.
Conducting assessments, audits, and monitoring to validate adherence to safety standards and identifying gaps or vulnerabilities.
Leading incident response readiness and coordinating response activities, ensuring compliance with defined safety and regulatory requirements.
Maintaining enterprise visibility of digital assets and establish appropriate classification, protection, and lifecycle management.

Governance, Compliance, and External Alignment
Overseeing and confirming alignment with regulatory requirements and maintain readiness for audits and inspections.
Building and maintaining relationships with regulatory bodies, industry organizations, and external experts.
Monitoring emerging threats, technologies, and regulatory changes, incorporating them into the Digital Safety Framework as appropriate.

Leadership and Organizational Capability
Leading and developing a high-performing team of digital safety professionals, fostering a culture of accountability, excellence, and continuous improvement.
Developing workforce capability plans to build and sustain the skills required to execute Digital Safety objectives.
Managing budgets, resources, and priorities to deliver on strategic Digital Safety objectives.

Other duties as assigned by your manager.

What We Are Looking For

Education
Bachelor's or Master's degree in cyber Security, Information Systems, Business Administration or related field, or equivalent work experience.
Relevant certifications (e.g., CISSP, CISM, ITIL) are highly desirable.

Experience
10+ years of experience in cyber security, with specific expertise in nuclear or critical infrastructure protection preferred.
10+ years in progressive leadership roles.
Demonstrated experience establishing and governing enterprise security or control frameworks.
Experience implementing and interpreting industry and regulatory standards (e.g., CSA N290.7, ISO 27001, NIST).
Proven ability to lead large-scale organizational transformation and embed control disciplines in complex environments.
Experience in operational technology (OT), industrial control systems (ICS), or SCADA environments strongly preferred.
Experience in managing budgets, strategic planning, and resource allocation.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities
Ability to define and communicate a clear Digital Safety vision and framework aligned to nuclear safety principles.
Strong understanding of defence-in-depth, risk-based control models, and safety-critical system governance.
Exceptional decision-making and judgement in high-risk and complex environments.
Ability to establish authority and enforce standards in environments with competing priorities.
Strong influencing and negotiation skills, particularly in cross-functional and non-hierarchical contexts.
Deep understanding of current and emerging cyber threats and mitigation strategies.
Ability to translate technical controls into clear, actionable safety requirements.
Strong leadership and people development capabilities.
Ability to drive behavioural and cultural change across a diverse workforce.
Excellent communication skills, including the ability to engage both technical and executive audiences.
Strong knowledge of:
CSA N290.7 (Nuclear Cyber Security)
ISO 27001
NIST Cybersecurity Framework
IAEA guidance and nuclear regulatory expectations
Familiarity with OT/ICS environments and digital instrumentation & control systems.
Understanding of how nuclear safety principles apply to digital systems.
Experience applying structured change management approaches (i.e., ADKAR).

Security Clearance Eligibility Required
Level 3 Secret requires a minimum of 10 years of verifiable history in Canada, Australia, New Zealand, the United States, and/or the United Kingdom. CNL implements security screening in accordance with the Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat's “Standard on Security Screening” and the “Policy on Government Security.”

Working Conditions

Working schedule: Five (5) days per week, seven and a half (7.5) hours per day for a thirty-seven and a half (37.5) hour work week.

Why CNL?

Does the idea of working with a dynamic team across Canada to advance nuclear science and technology for a clean and secure world
excite you? At CNL, we’re reinventing ourselves to be industry leaders— pioneering solutions to the problems that matter most
.

From building the next generation of clean nuclear and hydrogen energy technologies
, to developing targeted cancer treatments
, to continuing our global leadership in environmental remediation
—we are driven by impact, innovation, and purpose.

What We Offer: A Total Rewards Package

We believe in taking care of our people. Here’s what you can expect as part of our team:

Paid time off: vacation, sick, personal, and floater days
Benefits effective Day One – no waiting period
Tuition support to help you keep learning and growing
A defined-benefit pension plan or a defined-contribution pension plan, depending on your employee group, to support your long‑term financial security

Do Our Priorities Resonate with You?

Delivering clean energy for today and tomorrow
Restoring and protecting the environment
Contributing to the health of Canadians

If so, you’ll feel right at home at CNL!

Location: Fully Remote

This position is offered on a fully remote
basis, allowing you to work from home anywhere in Canada
. You’ll collaborate virtually with a dynamic team across CNL sites, helping to advance Canada’s clean energy and environmental goals from your home office.

Please note:
This is a remote position
supporting the Chalk River Laboratory, Ontario.

This individual will be responsible for owning end-to-end program delivery, managing executive stakeholder relationships, building high-performing delivery teams, and helping grow PwC's Microsoft consulting practice.

The successful candidate will combine deep expertise in Microsoft technologies, particularly Microsoft Azure and Microsoft AI Foundry, with proven experience leading large-scale enterprise transformation programs and offshore delivery organizations. This is a delivery-first leadership role focused on execution, client outcomes, and scaling delivery capabilities rather than pure sales or advisory responsibilities. Your role will include, but isn’t limited to:

Delivery Leadership & Program Ownership

Lead end-to-end delivery of large-scale Microsoft Data, AI, and Cloud transformation programs.
Own program outcomes including scope, budget, governance, risk management, quality, and delivery success.
Lead multiple concurrent programs and workstreams across complex enterprise environments.
Establish effective delivery governance, escalation management, and executive reporting structures.
Drive successful outcomes across strategic transformation initiatives and managed delivery engagements.

Microsoft Data & AI Transformation

Lead delivery of solutions leveraging: Microsoft Azure; Microsoft AI Foundry; Azure AI Services; Microsoft Fabric; Enterprise Data Platforms; Modern Analytics Solutions.
Support clients in cloud modernization, data platform transformation, and enterprise AI adoption initiatives.
Develop delivery roadmaps that align technology investments with business objectives and measurable outcomes.
Provide practical guidance on enterprise Data & AI transformation approaches and operating models.

Executive Stakeholder Management

Build trusted advisor relationships with CIOs, CTOs, Chief Data Officers, technology leaders, and business executives.
Represent PwC during executive steering committees, governance reviews, and program leadership meetings.
Serve as the primary delivery lead for strategic client engagements.
Communicate delivery status, risks, dependencies, and business impacts to executive stakeholders.
Facilitate decision-making across client, partner, and delivery teams.

Global Delivery & Offshore Leadership

Lead geographically distributed teams across Canada, the United States, and offshore delivery centres.
Manage complex global delivery models utilizing onshore and offshore resources.
Coordinate activities across delivery teams, vendors, architects, engineers, and business stakeholders.
Establish delivery practices that support scalability, quality, accountability, and operational excellence.
Drive issue resolution, risk mitigation, and program recovery efforts where required.

Talent Development & Practice Growth

Build and scale high-performing delivery teams.
Leverage professional networks to identify, attract, and develop top Microsoft delivery talent.
Mentor Managers, Senior Managers, Architects, and Delivery Leaders.
Foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, transparency, and continuous improvement.
Contribute to the ongoing growth of PwC's Microsoft Data & AI practice.

Business Development & Alliance Growth

Support pursuits, proposals, executive presentations, and solution development activities.
Build and strengthen relationships with Microsoft and key client stakeholders.
Contribute to thought leadership and market-facing initiatives related to Microsoft Data & AI solutions.
Help develop delivery offerings, accelerators, and go-to-market capabilities.
Support long-term practice growth and strategic expansion objectives.

What You'll Bring

Your skills, knowledge, and experiences are what set you apart. Here's what we look for:

12+ years of professional experience in technology consulting, enterprise transformation, cloud delivery, or technology leadership.
10+ years of experience leading large-scale enterprise technology programs and delivery organizations.
Proven experience delivering Microsoft-based transformation programs.
Strong experience with Microsoft Azure and modern Microsoft Data & AI technologies.
Extensive experience managing offshore and global delivery teams.
Demonstrated success managing executive-level stakeholder relationships and steering committees.
Experience leading large multidisciplinary teams across delivery, architecture, engineering, and business functions.
Strong consulting, stakeholder management, and client relationship management capabilities.
Experience owning complex budgets, delivery risks, resource plans, and program governance.
Demonstrated ability to independently lead large-scale client engagements with limited oversight.

This position ensures continuity and upholds our standards of excellence following the departure of a valued team member.

The salary range for this position is $191,200 - $241,200. The posted salary range represents the expected hiring range for PwC locations in major city centres. Given our national recruiting approach, ranges may vary for positions in other locations. At PwC Canada, base salary is determined by your skills, experience, qualifications and work location. In addition to base salary, eligible employees may have opportunities to participate in variable incentive pay programs which are designed to reward individual and firm-wide achievements. new_jobs.title: Vice President Finance, Americas
new_jobs.description:
The Vice President, Finance, Americas is responsible for providing strategic financial leadership and oversight across the Americas region. This role partners with executive and business leaders to drive financial performance, support growth initiatives, ensure compliance with financial and regulatory requirements, and deliver accurate financial planning, reporting, and analysis. The VP Finance leads regional finance functions, including accounting, budgeting, forecasting, tax, treasury, internal controls, and financial operations, while fostering a high-performing team and supporting the achievement of organizational objectives.

Reports to the Chief Financial Officer.

Responsibilities

1. Financial Reporting & Accounting

Oversee accounting operations for the Americas region, including general ledger, month-end/quarter-end closing, and consolidation.
Own inventory accounting for the Memphis distribution center — valuation methodology, standard costing, cycle counts, and obsolescence/reserve policy.
Ensure COGS accuracy and margin analysis tied to distribution operations.
Ensure accuracy of financial statements prepared in accordance with local GAAP in each jurisdiction (US, Canada, and LatAm countries).
Prepare and submit financial reports in compliance with IFRS and Group accounting standards, ensuring quality and compliance.
Coordinate with external auditors for annual audits, implement improvement plans, and maintain effective communication with internal and external audit teams.
Work closely with the HQ finance team to ensure consistency in reporting formats, policies, and processes.

2. Compliance

Maintain and enhance internal control and accounting procedures to align with Group policies and US/Canadian/LatAm regulations.
Ensure customs and bonded warehouse compliance — duty deferral, in-bond transfers, and CBP requirements — for the Memphis distribution center, partnering with trade compliance and logistics teams.
Ensure compliance with local direct and indirect tax regulations, including corporate income tax, VAT/GST, and multi-state US sales/use tax nexus; complete filings accurately and on time.
Regularly review the reasonableness of intercompany transfer pricing across US, Canada, and LatAm entities, and assess associated risks.

3. Treasury & Financial Planning

Manage cash flow, working capital, and banking relationships across the Americas to ensure liquidity and efficient funding.
Support financing activities and treasury optimization.
Provide budgeting, forecasting, and financial analysis to support operational decision-making across HQ, sales & marketing offices, and the distribution center.

4. System & Process Enhancement

Drive ERP system integration and automation to improve reporting efficiency, data accuracy, and close timelines.
Identify process improvement opportunities across order-to-cash and purchase-to-pay to enhance timeliness and reliability of financial information.

Qualifications and Experience

Bachelor's degree or above in Accounting, Finance, or related field; CPA/ACA/ACCA qualification preferred.
Minimum 15 years of accounting or finance experience, including at least 6 years in a managerial or Controller role.
Solid knowledge of IFRS, US/Canadian tax regulations, compliance, and internal controls.
Experience with distribution or logistics operations, including inventory accounting and customs/bonded warehouse environments, strongly preferred.
Hands-on SAP experience, particularly ERP implementation or migration, is a strong plus.
Previous experience in multinational or listed companies is a strong plus.
Proven leadership experience building and managing multi-country/multi-entity finance teams.
Strong written and verbal English communication skills for global stakeholder management. Chinese is a plus for Group-level communication.

Competencies (Skills & Behaviors)

Strong AI awareness with hands-on experience implementing AI tools or automation workflows within a finance environment.
Experience supporting regional or global finance functions.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Familiar with transfer pricing and cross-border tax principles.
Comfortable operating at senior leadership/executive committee level, with strong stakeholder management and influencing skills.
Familiar with inventory and sales/purchase management.

Leadership & Strategic Influence

Partner with Americas business, sales, and marketing leadership to provide financial insights, operational performance analysis, and cost control recommendations.
Build, lead, and develop a high-performing finance team across Montreal HQ, sales & marketing offices, and the Memphis distribution center; drive talent development and succession planning.
Act as a strategic finance partner to the Americas leadership team, contributing to regional business strategy, investment decisions, and capital allocation.
Report to the Group CFO on financial performance, risks, and strategic priorities, representing Americas Finance in Group-level executive discussions.

new_jobs.title: Director of Financial Planning and Analysis
new_jobs.description:
About the Company

Our client is a leading capital markets organization. They are looking for a Director, Corporate FP&A who will be responsible for leading the Corporate FP&A team responsible for enterprise planning, while also playing a key role in supporting Finance Business Partnering (FBP) teams.
In this leadership role, you empower financially sound planning and decision-making throughout the organization. You do this by spreading financial acumen, telling compelling, data-driven stories to spur action, bridging the knowledge gap between Finance and Operations, and assisting in the creation of FP&A decision-support tools. You will simplify FP&A analysis into easily digestible business logic and take a more technology-guided and teaching-focused approach to business partnering, enabling decision-makers to make sound financial decisions more independently

Requirements

CPA designation or similar (MBA/CFA)
10-15+ years of progressive finance experience with main focus in FP&A
Exposure to IFRS at a public listed entity
Strong business partnering with board reporting experience
Experience in a multi-entity environment with complex organization structures

Salary Range

$160,000 - $180,000/year

Why Work Here

High visibility with CEO, CFO and Board
Enterprise-wide impact as acquisitions has outpaced finance processes
This hire would ideally hit VPs succession map
Exposure to investor relations and strategic finance

About the Opportunity

Enterprise Planning

Ownership of forecasting and annual business planning across the group, including:
Coordination of timelines and assumption alignment across business units
Multi-stage reviews with senior leadership
Creation of final presentations for the Board of Directors
Ownership of Adaptive Planning (Workday Planning tool)
Lead the corporate target-setting process to optimize investment allocation while establishing achievable and stretch performance targets that drive desired behaviours and outcomes
Ownership of the long-term strategic forecast model used in the annual strategic planning process and longer-term modelling
Conduct business analysis on key enterprise performance drivers (e.g., headcount, profitability)

Corporate Performance Reporting

Accountable for corporate performance reporting to senior management and the Board of Directors, with a focus on forward-looking, actionable insights
Responsible for content creation, key messaging, and performance insights
Lead presentations of results to the Operating Committee
Accountable for operating segment reporting in external financial statements and MD&A
Partner closely with Investor Relations to synthesize monthly performance data into:
Quarterly earnings scripts
Q&A preparation materials
Analyst consensus models
Investor presentation metrics
Prepare supplementary schedules and analyze/proof quarterly and annual MD&A, press releases, Investor Relations presentations, and communications with shareholders and analysts
Partner closely with other Finance leaders and teams to improve data capture and GL reporting structures and optimize straight-through processing
Ownership of incentive plan performance measurement and associated liabilities across TMX; contribute to the design of incentive plans in partnership with HR

Enterprise Portfolio Governance

Oversee and recommend processes for annual and in-year discretionary investment allocations that balance governance, transparency, and business outcomes in alignment with TMX's growth strategy
Facilitate transparency for material new initiatives outside approved budgets to support CEO, CFO, and SMT approval decisions
Partner with the PMO and Integration Management Office on overall project governance and tracking
Co-owner of company-wide policies, including the TMX Expenditure and Budget Authorization Policy

Cost Allocation (Shared Services) Model

Ownership of the enterprise-wide cost allocation framework across legal entities and operating segments
Lead the design and structure of the model, including:
Tools
Principles
Governance
Regulatory compliance
Tax compliance
Provide detailed transparency to senior management and Business Unit FBPs regarding key drivers and outcomes, with a focus on understanding value delivery and influencing shared services costs
Provide variance analysis (budget vs. actual, prior period comparisons, etc.) in a manner that is easily understood by senior management
Support FBPs in stakeholder discussions to improve confidence in model integrity
Partner closely with team members to enhance data capture and GL reporting structures and improve straight-through processing
Conduct business analysis on key enterprise cost drivers
Enhance the rigour and control framework surrounding model updates and design
Build flexibility and adaptability into the model to accommodate a rapidly evolving corporate structure, including M&A activity
Collaborate with external auditors during quarterly reviews and annual audits
Improve efficiency of model updates and monthly/quarterly journal entries through automation where possible
Develop a roadmap for the next generation of the model and framework

Other

Ownership of quarterly and annual goodwill impairment testing and valuation processes, including:
Alignment with strategic plans
Input into external disclosure requirements
Partner with Corporate Strategy and Strategic Finance teams to advance enterprise analysis and insight generation
Champion and participate in knowledge-sharing forums for FBPs and FP&A professionals to exchange best practices on educating business leaders through FP&A decision-support processes
Assist in defining success criteria for FP&A tools and establishing measurable business and technical metrics to monitor utilization and quality

How to Apply

Click the “Apply Now” button and follow the instructions to submit your resume. Please know that we only accept documents in MS Word or Rich Text formats.

new_jobs.title: Director, Digital Safety
new_jobs.description:
Are you looking for a role where you can define the future of digital safety in a complex, mission-critical environment? Can you see yourself leading enterprise-wide cybersecurity programs while establishing the standards, controls, and governance frameworks that protect critical digital systems and information assets? If you answered yes, this may be the job for you. Apply today,
as our Chalk River location is looking for a Director, Digital Safety
to lead the development and implementation of CNL's Digital Safety Framework.

What you will be doing!

Digital Safety Framework & Standards Authority
Defining, maintaining, and evolving the enterprise Digital Safety Framework, incorporating nuclear safety principles such as defence-in-depth, graded approach, and continuous improvement.
Establishing and governing mandatory, non-negotiable digital safety control requirements applicable to:
Information systems
Operational technologies
Nuclear-related digital assets
Identity and access managemen
Data protection and asset lifecycle management

Translating external standards (CSA N290.7, ISO 27001, NIST, IAEA) into a cohesive, internally consistent Digital Safety Framework.
Defining the baseline conditions required for safe digital operations, ensuring clarity in expectations across all business and operational areas.

Program Implementation
Embedding Digital Safety requirements into all business processes, projects, and operational activities to obtain compliance with defined safety standards.
Developing and delivering enterprise-wide programs to build digital safety awareness, competency, and behavioural accountability.
Driving the integration of human factors and behavioural science into digital safety practices, reinforcing safe decision-making and risk-awareness across the workforce.
Promoting and enforcing understanding so that all employees and contractors understand their role in maintaining digital safety and operate within defined safety expectations.

Control Oversight and Operational Assurance
Exercising authority to mandate that all digital systems and activities comply with established Digital Safety requirements.
Conducting assessments, audits, and monitoring to validate adherence to safety standards and identifying gaps or vulnerabilities.
Leading incident response readiness and coordinating response activities, ensuring compliance with defined safety and regulatory requirements.
Maintaining enterprise visibility of digital assets and establish appropriate classification, protection, and lifecycle management.

Governance, Compliance, and External Alignment
Overseeing and confirming alignment with regulatory requirements and maintain readiness for audits and inspections.
Building and maintaining relationships with regulatory bodies, industry organizations, and external experts.
Monitoring emerging threats, technologies, and regulatory changes, incorporating them into the Digital Safety Framework as appropriate.

Leadership and Organizational Capability
Leading and developing a high-performing team of digital safety professionals, fostering a culture of accountability, excellence, and continuous improvement.
Developing workforce capability plans to build and sustain the skills required to execute Digital Safety objectives.
Managing budgets, resources, and priorities to deliver on strategic Digital Safety objectives.

Other duties as assigned by your manager.

What We Are Looking For

Education
Bachelor's or Master's degree in cyber Security, Information Systems, Business Administration or related field, or equivalent work experience.
Relevant certifications (e.g., CISSP, CISM, ITIL) are highly desirable.

Experience
10+ years of experience in cyber security, with specific expertise in nuclear or critical infrastructure protection preferred.
10+ years in progressive leadership roles.
Demonstrated experience establishing and governing enterprise security or control frameworks.
Experience implementing and interpreting industry and regulatory standards (e.g., CSA N290.7, ISO 27001, NIST).
Proven ability to lead large-scale organizational transformation and embed control disciplines in complex environments.
Experience in operational technology (OT), industrial control systems (ICS), or SCADA environments strongly preferred.
Experience in managing budgets, strategic planning, and resource allocation.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities
Ability to define and communicate a clear Digital Safety vision and framework aligned to nuclear safety principles.
Strong understanding of defence-in-depth, risk-based control models, and safety-critical system governance.
Exceptional decision-making and judgement in high-risk and complex environments.
Ability to establish authority and enforce standards in environments with competing priorities.
Strong influencing and negotiation skills, particularly in cross-functional and non-hierarchical contexts.
Deep understanding of current and emerging cyber threats and mitigation strategies.
Ability to translate technical controls into clear, actionable safety requirements.
Strong leadership and people development capabilities.
Ability to drive behavioural and cultural change across a diverse workforce.
Excellent communication skills, including the ability to engage both technical and executive audiences.
Strong knowledge of:
CSA N290.7 (Nuclear Cyber Security)
ISO 27001
NIST Cybersecurity Framework
IAEA guidance and nuclear regulatory expectations
Familiarity with OT/ICS environments and digital instrumentation & control systems.
Understanding of how nuclear safety principles apply to digital systems.
Experience applying structured change management approaches (i.e., ADKAR).

Security Clearance Eligibility Required
Level 3 Secret requires a minimum of 10 years of verifiable history in Canada, Australia, New Zealand, the United States, and/or the United Kingdom. CNL implements security screening in accordance with the Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat's “Standard on Security Screening” and the “Policy on Government Security.”

Working Conditions

Working schedule: Five (5) days per week, seven and a half (7.5) hours per day for a thirty-seven and a half (37.5) hour work week.

Why CNL?

Does the idea of working with a dynamic team across Canada to advance nuclear science and technology for a clean and secure world
excite you? At CNL, we’re reinventing ourselves to be industry leaders— pioneering solutions to the problems that matter most
.

From building the next generation of clean nuclear and hydrogen energy technologies
, to developing targeted cancer treatments
, to continuing our global leadership in environmental remediation
—we are driven by impact, innovation, and purpose.

What We Offer: A Total Rewards Package

We believe in taking care of our people. Here’s what you can expect as part of our team:

Paid time off: vacation, sick, personal, and floater days
Benefits effective Day One – no waiting period
Tuition support to help you keep learning and growing
A defined-benefit pension plan or a defined-contribution pension plan, depending on your employee group, to support your long‑term financial security

Do Our Priorities Resonate with You?

Delivering clean energy for today and tomorrow
Restoring and protecting the environment
Contributing to the health of Canadians

If so, you’ll feel right at home at CNL!

Location: Fully Remote

This position is offered on a fully remote
basis, allowing you to work from home anywhere in Canada
. You’ll collaborate virtually with a dynamic team across CNL sites, helping to advance Canada’s clean energy and environmental goals from your home office.

Please note:
This is a remote position
supporting the Chalk River Laboratory, Ontario.

Our Commitment to Equity, Diversity & Inclusion

At CNL, we are committed to fostering an environment that promotes equity, diversity, and inclusion
. We celebrate and welcome employees, stakeholders, and partners of all backgrounds and identities. Click here to read all about it!

:

Teamwork

for all employees.
